title: Echinopsis Atacamensis and the Milky Way
caption: Cacti beneath the Milky Way near ALMA, Chajnantor, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at ALMA, Chajnantor plateau, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Tall cacti stand beneath the Milky Way, which is on full display across the sky. In the lower right glows the Large Magellanic Cloud. Stéphane Guisard captured this view in the Chilean Atacama Desert.

The spot lies along the winding road that connects the ALMA Operation Support Facility, at 3,000m, to the Array Operation Site, 5,000m up. Between about 3500m and 3800m, the landscape is dominated by large cacti of the species Echinopsis atacamensis.

These plants grow slowly, on average about 1cm per year, yet they can reach heights of up to 9m. Such slow growth means the tallest plants are very old. They stand as landmarks of the high desert beneath the band of our own galaxy.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera on the road to ALMA. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure collects much more light than the eye, so the Milky Way and the Large Magellanic Cloud look brighter and more detailed than they would in person.

explore: The Large Magellanic Cloud is a small companion galaxy of the Milky Way, visible from the Southern Hemisphere as a hazy patch separate from the main band.
alt: Tall cacti in the desert beneath the Milky Way, with the Large Magellanic Cloud in the lower right of the sky.
